title: Phosphorus was discovered by an alchemist boiling urine
body: In 1669 the Hamburg alchemist Hennig Brand was hunting for the philosopher’s stone, the legendary substance that would turn base metals into gold. He experimented with urine, which contains plenty of dissolved phosphates, and after much heating obtained a waxy white substance that **glowed in the dark**. He had found phosphorus, the first element discovered since antiquity. The name means ‘light-bearer’ in Greek, after the morning star; the glow is not phosphorescence at all but chemiluminescence, light given off as white phosphorus slowly reacts with the air.

steps.label: Let urine stand, then boil it to a paste
Distil the paste at a high temperature
A waxy white solid that glows in the dark

slides.heading: Light-bearer
slides.text: Phosphorus comes from the Greek phōsphoros, ‘light-bearer’, a name for the morning star, the planet Venus shining before sunrise. Exposed to air, white phosphorus faintly glows green and blue as it oxidises.

left.label: Phosphorescence
left.text: Stored light released slowly, like glow-in-the-dark stars. Named after phosphorus, but not what phosphorus does.

right.label: Chemiluminescence
right.text: Light made by a chemical reaction. White phosphorus glows because it is slowly reacting with the air.

slides.heading: Why urine
slides.text: Phosphorus is in every cell: in DNA, RNA, ATP and the phospholipids of cell membranes, and bone mineral is a form of calcium phosphate. The body sheds phosphates in urine, so Brand’s unappealing raw material was a decent source.

slides.question: Your body holds about 0.7 kg of phosphorus. Out of every 10 grams, how many are in your bones and teeth?
slides.explanation: About 85 to 90%, as apatite, the calcium phosphate mineral of bone and tooth enamel. The rest is spread through soft tissues and body fluids, in DNA, ATP and cell membranes.

slides.question: What was Hennig Brand actually trying to make?
slides.explanation: He hoped to turn base metals into gold and worked with urine, which is rich in dissolved phosphates. Instead he isolated a glowing new element.
